source.title: Isolated Mononeuropathy From Rucksack Palsy: A Case Series

semantic_spot_checks.claim: Case 2 symptoms followed a 13-mile march with an older internal-frame pack loaded to 65 pounds.
At five months, Case 2 could perform 91 push-ups but still had disproportionate right-sided fatigue.
The authors say conclusions about modern pack superiority are mostly anecdotal.
Table I summarizes one spinal accessory neuropathy and two long thoracic neuropathies with the expected lateral versus medial winging patterns.
The conclusion calls isolated rucksack-associated mononeuropathy under-recognized and says it most commonly affects the LTN and SAN.

source_integrity_notes: The article has no formal Methods section. The extraction does not invent a standardized enrollment, intervention, comparator, or outcome protocol.
Secondary incidence, biomechanical strap, and framed-versus-frameless results are preserved as the case-series authors reports of cited studies and tagged secondary_reported_result.

The source text for Case 1 says trapezius EMG showed mildly reduced recruitment, while Table I renders the upper-trapezius EMG summary differently. Both source locations are preserved rather than silently harmonized.
Model-extracted atoms remain needs_review because no independent human reviewer is recorded in atom provenance. Packet-level verification is recorded separately by this audit.
